journey.howSecured:
1. Online MCQ Test (23/07/2025) – HackerEarth 
• Number of Candidates Appeared: 92 
• This round was conducted on HackerEarth and consisted of 20 multiple-choice questions to be 
solved in 90 minutes. 
• Topics included: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, DBMS, Computer Networks. 
• The questions were fairly easy and mostly based on fundamentals. 
• Shortlisted Candidates: 11 
(Note: 4 candidates had offers from Barclays and IDFC, so they did not appear for further 
rounds.) 
 
2. Machine Coding Round (30/07/2025) – BrowserStack Mumbai Office 
• Number of Candidates Appeared: 7 
This problem requires you to implement a log watching solution (similar to the tail -f command 
in UNIX). However, in this case, the log file is hosted on a remote machine (same machine as 
your server code). 
The log file is in append-only mode. 
You may implement the server in any programming language. 
You have to implement the following: 
1. A server side program to monitor the given log file and capable of streaming updates 
that happen in it. This will run on the same machine as the log file. 
2. A web based client (accessible via URL like http://localhost/log) that prints the updates 
in the file as and when they happen and NOT upon page refresh. The page should be 
loaded once and it should keep getting updated in real-time. 
3. The user sees the last 10 lines in the file when they visit the page for the first time. 
Problem Constraints 
Please read these thoroughly 
 The server should push updates to the clients as we have to be as real time as possible. 
Do this by Websokets in node you can use socket.io 
 Be aware that the log file may be several GB, how to optimise for retrieving the last 10 
lines – Use list of last 10 lines and updates it when file changes and read file in reverse 
and load small chunk in buffer instead of loading complete file. 
 The server should not retransmit the entire file every time. It should only send the 
updates.  – Create event update (to get new lines) init (to get last 10 lines) 
 The server should be able to handle multiple clients at the same time. 
 They will be evaluating you for working solution, code efficiency, corner cases, etc 
 For more info visit this – Log Watcher Solution 
• After this round, a lunch break was given, and then results were announced. 
• Shortlisted candidate - 3 
 
Instead of selected, they call out the names of those who are not selected. If your name isn't 
called, you've made it to the next round. 
 
 
3. Technical + HR Interview (30/07/2025) – BrowserStack Mumbai Office 
• Number of Candidates Appeared: 3 
• The interview began with a short introduction from both sides. 
• Then we had an in-depth discussion about my project—why I built it, the tech stack used, and 
the reasoning behind the choices and features of project lasted about 20 minutes. 
Technical Questions Asked: 
1. Next Greater Element – Using monotonic stack. 
2. SQL vs NoSQL – Differences and use cases with real life example. 
3. Process vs Thread – Why processes are needed if threads exist. 
4. Troubleshooting – What to do if a website doesn't open or internet isn't working tell me 
all options for troubleshoot. 
5. 10 TB File Problem – 
o Problem: Find the word “programmer” in a 10 TB file 
o My approach: 
 Initially said I’d read the file and search line by line 
 Interviewer pointed out memory limitations 
 Then I proposed dividing the file into blocks 
 They raised a concern: the word may split across blocks (e.g., ‘prog’ and 
‘rammer’) 
 I suggested using buffer overlap between blocks 
 Also mentioned using multiple threads for parallel processing 
At the end, they asked if I had any questions. I asked, 
"If I get selected, what would a typical day at BrowserStack look like?" 
 
Result: 
The next day, HR informed me and another one that I had been selected.                                   
Next week they added one more to shortlisted list.                                                                         
Total Candidates Offered: 3 
 
Placement Preparation Tips 
1. Start Early with Core Subjects 
Begin your placement preparation as early as possible. Focus on fundamental computer science 
subjects such as DBMS, Operating Systems, Computer Networks, and Object-Oriented 
Programming (OOPs). 
Make concise, revision-friendly notes for these subjects to help during the last-minute prep. 
Also, research frequently asked interview questions to become familiar with recurring patterns 
and concepts. 
 
 
 
2. Resume 
Your resume should reflect your actual knowledge and experience. Avoid adding skills or 
technologies that you cannot explain if asked in the interview it may come off as dishonest and 
create a negative impression. 
At the very least, ensure you understand the basic concepts of everything mentioned. Tailor 
your resume slightly depending on the specific role you're applying for . 
 
3. Pay Attention to the Company Presentation 
The first step in most placement processes is usually a company presentation. 
Be attentive and note important details about the company’s history, products, services, and 
culture. If you have doubts about the roles and responsibilities, clarify them early. This will help 
you make an informed decision and also position yourself as someone who is genuinely 
interested in the company. 
 
4. Practice is Key for Online Assessments 
For Online Assessments (OAs), consistent practice can make a big difference. 
Participate in coding contests and take timed tests to improve your problem solving speed and 
accuracy. This will also help you identify your weak areas and improve over time. 
 
5. Approach Interviews Calmly and Confidently 
In interviews, focus on explaining your approach clearly rather than jumping to give the right 
answer immediately. Interviewers are more interested in your thought process and problem-
solving skills. 
Staying calm and confident shows that you can perform under pressure, which is an essential 
trait for any role. 
 
6. Stay Positive and Keep Improving 
Finally, don’t lose hope if things don’t go as planned. Focus on how you can improve your 
chances of getting selected. 
Understand your strengths and weaknesses, and keep refining them throughout the placement 
season. Persistence and continuous improvement are key. 
 You should give 60% time for DSA and 40% for Projects building. 
 You can’t do only dsa or projects you need to do both. 
 Try to give leetcode or codeforces weekly contest so you will learn time management. 
 This was my 3rd Inteview I saw my friends gave more interviews than and not selected 
so be patient so keep grinding you will definitely get results. 
 It is not too late or early start hardwork from as soon as possible. 
 Please don’t cheat in placement process it will affect whole college due to you. 
 In placements, luck plays a major role. Here's how I would break it down: 
 
Stage Skills Luck Communication/Approach

Interview 50% 30% 20%
